newsitem.title: USA: Kodak shares fall on U.S. pricing concerns.
newsitem.headline: Kodak shares fall on U.S. pricing concerns.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co. stock fell sharply Wednesday amid concern that it faces severe pricing pressure in the U.S. film market from Japan's Fuji Photo Film Co.

Competition with Fuji could portend a "real pricing war," said Alexander Henderson, an analyst at Prudential Securities. He estimates Kodak may have lost 3 percent to 4 percent of the share the U.S. market for 35 mm film so far this year to Fuji.

Fuji is so aggressive with its film pricing in the United States that even private label film -- which is typically priced between 40 percent and 50 percent below name brands -- is feeling the squeeze.
"This is a yellow flag on Kodak," Henderson said. "We're very concerned."
Kodak's stock closed down $4.375, or 5.22 percent, at $79.50. More than 3.2 million shares traded hands on the New York Stock Exchange.

In terms of market share, "Kodak lost 4.5 percentage points for the four weeks ended May 17, and Fuji gained it all," said Brenda Landry, an analyst at Morgan Stanley, who cited retail sales data from a variety of sources, including Information Resources Inc.

Kodak may also face pressure on its domestic market share during the second quarter, including pressure on domestic market share for photographic paper, said Salomon Brothers analyst Jonathan Rosenzweig.
He added that the company's consumer business seemed less upbeat than its emerging markets business. He said Salomon would maintain its "hold" rating on Kodak's stock.

"Although we are not changing our forecasts at this time, it is relevant to note that our model previously called for consumer imaging margins to turn up in the third quarter," Rosenzweig said in a report.
Kodak officials said they had no immediate comment on the company's U.S. market share data and knew no reason for the stock's decline.
